headline: Soy Compound Shows Promise in Protecting Brain from Salt Damage
meta_description: Japanese researchers found that LPC70, a soy-derived compound, protected mice from high blood pressure and memory problems linked to excessive salt consumption.
summary_short: A natural soy compound helped mice recover memory and social skills lost to high-salt diets, opening new research paths for protecting human brains.
body:
Japanese researchers have identified a promising natural shield against the brain damage caused by excessive salt. Working with a soy-derived compound called LPC70, scientists at Fujita Health University discovered that mice supplemented with this ingredient recovered lost memory and improved their social interactions—effects that disappeared when they consumed too much salt alone. The mice also showed better blood pressure control. The findings, published in Neurochemistry International in July 2026, reveal that high-salt diets do far more than raise blood pressure; they selectively harm complex cognitive and social functions, leaving basic movement and anxiety responses largely unchanged.

Prof. Akihiro Mouri's team studied how LPC70 works at the molecular level, focusing on prostaglandins—chemical signals that act like local hormones throughout the body. In the kidneys, excess salt triggers harmful changes in these signaling pathways that drive hypertension. LPC70 reversed those changes. In the prefrontal cortex, the brain region governing memory and social behavior, the compound restored protective signaling without triggering harmful pathways. This selective action distinguishes LPC70 from blunt treatments that simply suppress all activity: it appears to fine-tune the brain's chemical balance rather than sledgehammer it.

The research emerged from collaboration between Fujita Health University and Tsuji Oil Mills Co., Ltd., which develops naturally derived food ingredients. While the study involved mice, not humans, the specificity of LPC70's protective effects hints at why it could eventually benefit people struggling with both hypertension and cognitive decline linked to dietary salt. As salt consumption remains a major public health concern worldwide, finding natural compounds that address both cardiovascular and brain damage offers a genuinely hopeful research direction.
quick_facts: Japanese researchers at Fujita Health University tested LPC70, a soy-derived compound
LPC70 improved blood pressure, memory, and social behavior in salt-fed mice
Compound works by restoring protective signaling in the brain's prefrontal cortex
High-salt diets harm memory and social skills more than general behavior
